clue.text: He cannot possibly work at an atomic level

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of these two words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone protests that he is unable to do fine-scale work involving atoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange HECANNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for nanotechnology, engineering carried out on the scale of molecules and individual atoms.

clue.text: Inferior people love a runner-up

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, a round O

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for runner reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a ski is a runner that slides over snow

explanation.surface: Snobbish talk dismissing lesser folk, who love a second-place finisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner-up' looks like one word for second place; split it into 'runner' and 'up'. 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang put-down for uncouth, lower-class people, so a scornful name for inferiors.

clue.text: Tedious recital in Italy, round about noon

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other, enclosing it
round suggests the letters of the country name being turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A dull speech given in Italy at about midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' scrambles ITALY to LITAY, and 'about' puts it around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long repetitive list or account, hence a boring recitation.

clue.text: Female artist agreed pay rise before pay cut

parts.note: OK means agreed

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise says the word for pay reads upwards

parts.note: a fee is a payment

indicators.note: cut says the word for pay loses its last letter

parts.note: again a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A woman painter, having agreed a raise, then takes a reduction in salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns FEE to EEF; 'cut' trims the second FEE to FE.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia O'Keeffe was an American painter famous for her flowers and desert landscapes, so a woman artist.

clue.text: Pay special attention to extended part of northern bridge

definitions.text: Pay special attention to extended part of northern bridge

parts.words: Pay special attention to extended part of northern bridge
parts.note: the abbreviation NB, read as N for northern and B for bridge, written out in full gives a Latin phrase meaning note well

explanation.surface: A warning to look carefully at the longer section of a bridge in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forth Bridge, the puzzle's theme, is a northern bridge; NB extended is the Latin phrase it abbreviates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means note well, an instruction to pay particular attention.

clue.text: Scottish bible's including Edinburgh's top sources of tourist info

indicators.note: including says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: the Bible is the Good Book; Scots say guid for good

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of the city name

explanation.surface: A Scottish holy book takes in Edinburgh's finest sights for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guid' is Scots for good, and the Good Book is the Bible; 'including' takes in the 'top' of Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidebooks give visitors information about places to see, so they are sources for travellers.

clue.text: More convenient point at which to get a rise negotiated

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: negotiated suggests the words a rise being worked into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking when it would be handier to get a pay increase agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' is the anagram signal, not about pay talks; 'at which to get' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of easy: something less difficult is handier or more convenient.

clue.text: Obsequious hotel owner is known primarily as a legendary slitherer

parts.note: Basil Fawlty, the fawning-to-the-posh hotelier in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A grovelling innkeeper is best known as a mythical snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil Fawlty runs a hotel in the British TV comedy Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: The basilisk is a mythical serpent that could kill with a glance, so a fabled creature that slithers.

clue.text: Like the Eye, inclined to jest? No honour in that

indicators.note: No says the honour card is removed from the word for joking

parts.note: jocular means given to joking
the jack is an honour card in bridge, abbreviated J

explanation.surface: Asks whether the London Eye is playful, with no honour involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop J from JOCULAR. 'in that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to eyes, so pertaining to the eye.

clue.text: Nothing works? Sorry, my mistake

parts.note: nothing is zero, O
ops is short for opuses, musical works

explanation.surface: Someone finds nothing functioning and apologises for their error.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of apology uttered on making a blunder.

clue.text: Running rail ad about cutback at northern country's second largest city

indicators.note: about says one piece surrounds the other
running suggests the letters of rail ad in motion and reshuffled

parts.note: cut is axe; back says to read it in reverse

explanation.surface: A railway advertisement criticising cuts in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' rearranges RAILAD to ALDRIA, which goes 'about' EXA (AXE turned 'back') plus N. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria is Egypt's second city, after Cairo, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Top or lower

definitions.meaning: a pullover or sweater worn on the upper body
something that lows, i.e. a cow, from the Channel Island breed

explanation.surface: Choosing between upper and bottom garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not 'below' but one that lows: a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a knitted pullover and a breed of dairy cow from the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Many turn over after sorry saga involving Sue Barker

indicators.note: after says those pieces come later in the answer
sorry, meaning in a poor state, suggests the letters being jumbled

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number

indicators.note: over says the word for turn is flipped

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A long tale about a woman named Sue Barker, apparently a turn-over by many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' looks like the tennis player and presenter Sue Barker, but it is the definition: a dog. SAGA with SUE rearranged gives SAUSAGE; GO turned 'over' gives OG.
explanation.definitionFit: A barker is a dog, and the long-bodied dachshund is nicknamed this in Britain.

clue.text: Forth Rail express starts at York — train finally arriving, when not bound to be so?

definitions.text: when not bound to be so

indicators.note: starts picks the first letters of the three words that follow

parts.note: Ebor is the abbreviated Latin name for York, from Eboracum

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An express on the Forth rail line stops at York with the train finally arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' and 'arriving' are links. The Forth Bridge, opened in 1890, is the puzzle's anniversary theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born free rather than into slavery or bondage is described this way.

clue.text: Divinely shaped "magic" model? Her guy's knocked out

parts.note: the Model T Ford, so model gives T

indicators.note: knocked out suggests the letters are battered into a new shape

parts.note: the words her guy, the 's being is

explanation.surface: A model's partner has been flattened by some divine magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' is the anagram signal; the Model T was the famous early Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: Theurgy is magic worked through divine or supernatural agency, as in ritual invocation of gods.

clue.text: We must employ rail worker, possibly a Scot

parts.note: a guard works on a railway train
Ian is a typical Scottish name, so one example of a Scot

explanation.surface: A firm must hire a railway employee, maybe someone from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We' is the newspaper this puzzle appears in. 'must employ' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper publishing the puzzle refers to itself in the first person plural.

clue.text: Make merry, as lyricist bags English girl

indicators.note: bags says the lyricist holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: Tim Rice wrote lyrics for Lloyd Webber musicals
Jo is a common girl's name

explanation.surface: Celebrate as a songwriter wins an English girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to celebrate or be glad, much like making merry.

clue.text: Needing some lifting gear, use a crane to find breaks in lines

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting says the run is read upwards
some says only a run of letters within these words is wanted

explanation.surface: To find gaps you need lifting equipment: use a crane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes EARUSEAC from 'gear, use a crane'; 'lifting' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesurae are pauses or breaks in the middle of lines of verse.

clue.text: Southeastern rail trips by one from another country

indicators.note: trips suggests the letters stumbling into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Train journeys on the Southeastern line, taken by a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' rearranges SERAIL to ISRAEL. Southeastern is also a British rail operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes someone or something belonging to Israel, a nation other than Britain.

clue.text: It's always found in first of acrosses and downs? Wrong this time!

indicators.note: found in says the word for always sits inside the following letters
wrong says the assembled letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged
first of picks the first letter of acrosses

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A puzzle remark: the answer is usually in the first clues, but not now.
explanation.walkthrough: AY 'found in' A plus DOWNS; 'Wrong' then rearranges all those letters. 'It's' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in the present era, at the current time, as opposed to the past.

clue.text: Coughs? Have a little drink

parts.note: to own is to have
a sup is a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: Suffering from a cough? Take a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coughs' is British slang for confesses, not a symptom.
explanation.definitionFit: To cough is slang for to confess, and owning up is admitting guilt.

clue.text: Part of Greek isle visited for third month of 19?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a Greek island visited during an Israeli month.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition began with 'for', which is a link; the definition is 'third month of 19', where 19 is ISRAELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Kislev is the third month of the Jewish civil year, used in Israel.

clue.text: Principal residence in a remote area?

parts.note: key means main or principal
pad is slang for someone's home

explanation.surface: A main home located in an isolated place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remote' is a TV remote control, not a far-off place. 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttons on a remote control form a pad of keys, a region of the device.

clue.text: Danny fiddled with one rice bomb

indicators.note: fiddled with says these letters are tampered with and reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Danny tampered with a single grain of rice.
explanation.definitionFit: An incendiary is a device designed to start fires, a type of explosive.

clue.text: Stick with sled that's good going west

indicators.note: going west says the letter for good moves to the left, the front, of the word

parts.note: a luge is a racing sled

explanation.surface: Stay on a sled, which is good for heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue is an adhesive, so it sticks; as a verb it means to stick.

clue.text: Somewhat ugly name for a Welshman

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rather an unattractive name to give a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', which is a link word, so the definition is just 'a Welshman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glyn is a typically Welsh male name, so it can stand for a man from Wales.

clue.text: Dawn French at the right, or away at the left

parts.note: au is French for at the
A stands for away in football results

explanation.surface: Comedian Dawn French on the right, or away on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn French' looks like the British comedian, but 'Dawn' is the definition and 'French' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the Latin name for the goddess of the dawn, and a poetic word for daybreak.

clue.text: A player sadly taking last place in the quadrennial event

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters are in a sorry, disordered state
last place in picks the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A competitor unhappily comes last in the Olympics, held every four years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges APLAYER with E. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A year with an extra day, February 29th, comes around once every four years.
